questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Argentina?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Argentina article.

questions.proof: In eastern Argentina is Buenos Aires, the capital of Argentina, it is also one of the largest cities in the world.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Argentina?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Argentina on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Argentina article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by Paraguay and Bolivia in the north, Brazil and Uruguay in the northeast, and Chile in the west and south.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Argentina?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Argentina article.

questions.proof: Spanish is the most spoken language, and the official language, but many other languages are spoken.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It also claims the Falkland Islands (Spanish: Islas Malvinas) and South _____ and the South Sandwich Islands.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “South”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Argentina article.

questions.proof: It also claims the Falkland Islands (Spanish: Islas Malvinas) and South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In the Americas (South and North), _____, US, Brazil and Argentina are the largest countries (in that order).”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “North”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Argentina article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: In the Americas (South and North), Canada, US, Brazil and Argentina are the largest countries (in that order).
